Complaint of comm failure. On arrival the machine was in operation. Found the LEN access plug at the connection board was broken and bent. The board must be replaced. Also found that the fan maximum was set to 40%. I released the fan to normal operation with the SP setpoint at 1in. The pressure tube had been pinched and kinked. The customer will repair. Ran the unit in test. Operation appears normal at this time. Note that the unit is connected to an EMS.  Replaced faulty CCN communication board. Verify connectivity. No other communication problems found at this time.
Replace the scrolling marquee and test operation.

disconnect was found bad during start up of equipment

Checked in. Brought tools to roof. Customer explained that the unit had a lot of condensation in the unit causing water build up and leaking into space. After thoroughly going over unit, I found 3 main issues. The first issue was the economizer hood was not connected at the bottom. There were screws missing allowing hood to move. Second, was a space between the unit and curb adaptor. Lastly, which I believe is the major issue, is there is no gas piping leaving a hole between burner section and suction side of supply fan. Tech in site explained that the inlet gas piping hole from the out side of unit was also open until they covered it when they had issue. Did not find any other issues. Brought tools down. Checked out.
Checked into front gate for base access. Arrived on job site inspected equipment and blower wheel all runs smoothly found no problems. Will start up equipment.

Fan had moved down the shaft and was rubbing against the fan shroud. Re-centered the blower wheel and tightened the set screws. Test ran by having Maxair adjust control settings to open terminal boxes. Fan speed went up to 80% with no abnormal vibration.

Rtu #27 repair. Customer called saying here was no heat coming from unit. Checked in with customer and went to unit. After connecting to unit I found that it had multiple alarms for loss of communication A175. Rest and started going through book to see what alarm goes too. Unit came up and ran for about 15 minutes and it throw out the same alarm again. Alarm is referring to loss of communication with the VFD. Checked the VFD for alarms and it had a 2005 alarm on it. With through and verified that the parameters are set correctly still. Turned power off to unit and climbed in it to check the wiring. After all that checked out I powered the unit back up. Unit start and ran for a hour and half with no issue. Released unit to customer. Going to suggest if it happens again we replace the wiring on from the VFD to MBB. Checked off site and cleaned up work area.

leaking unit - both circuits low to no charge after leaking checking and troubleshooting found that the  txv equalizer lines were crossed.  troubleshoot,  pulled charge, patched leak, leak checked, corrected equalizer lines, recharged, verified operational.

On site for start up. Had issue with vfd displaying drive not responding. Checked out vfd. Drive itself working ok. Verified through confortlink software.   Called in for support to Abb.   Case number 403717. Determined that display alarm was caused by bad connection from keypad to drive. Fixed issue. Display communication now ok.

Arrived on site.   Met with customer.   Troubleshot RTU 6 alarming in low suction temps.   Found supply fan VFD faulting in no start signal.   Found loose connection.   Resecured & reset VFD.   Equipment is back online & functioning properly.   Job is complete.
blower bearing was found blown out on diagnostic call
FAILED BEARINGS LOUD GRINDING NOISE , REPLACED BEARINGS FOR NORMAL QUIET OPERATION

Came out to job and found drive in alarm.found wire loose on drive.megged the motor and ohmed it out and it was good.cut wires back and hooked up the drive and checked configuration on it.ran unit and it???s running fine.unit has 217 hrsand 91 starts
WHY - areas not cooling   FOUND - motor grounded    DONE - replace motor

Arrived onsite and checked in and hauled tools on rooftop. Assessed unit and found over condensation in heater compartment. Checked and found air leaks not air locked by factory in heater compartment. Waiting for parts to insulate compartment.

Arrived on site checked rtu - unit tripping on rollout . Checked gas pressure . Checked ok . Re set unit checked operation.. Found flame to be rolling out. Checked area in burner section . Found supply air to leaking thru at higher speed causing rollout. Re sealed area with high temp silicon.   Re checked operation . Ok at this time.

Replaced stage control board as needed, and cut JMP3 & JMP8 jumpers to match the original configuration. Applied power and observed unit energize in Vent mode with low speed fan. Attempted to access the unit via BacNet, but unable to do so at this time. Discussed with Charlie S to follow up and adjust set points for seasonal change-over. Operation is normal.

Found actuators on economizer dampers were switched. Had to change serial numbers in controller and change rotation switch.  Dampers were operating in reverse from intended design. OA was open when commanded shut and RA was closed when commanded open. After attempting to solve issue on my own, I had to call Dan Kenyon for support. I couldn???t swap actuator serial numbers. We discovered that they had to first be zeroed then entered properly. Also rotation switch had to be changed.

Disabled the unit; removed the double-wall blower access panels ; drilled the rivet impact points; installed additional gasket; reinstalled the access panels; re-enabled the unit and observed the start-up.

Water is seeping into the space and running ceiling tiles.
